pr_title: Wait for task on master in testGetMappingsCancellation
pr_body:
Enable more logging to verify whether `assertAllCancellableTasksAreCancelled ` is able to always see the cancellable tasks. Also, ensure the task to be cancelled is already on the master to mitigate the cases where a quick cancellation cleans up tasks before the assertion is able to verify their existence.

Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/91248

comments:
Fortunately, there are some trace logs in this failure. Last time for a similar failure that shares some code with this we just increased timeout and log level (https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/88884). However, the log messages I've added is inaccurate and when in the log you see:
```
[testGetMappingsCancellation] --> found task with prefix [indices:admin/mappings/get] marked as cancelled: [org.elasticsearch.tasks.CancellableTask@26fb7fa]
```
It doesn't mean we have actually verified that the task is marked as cancellable but rather just that we have seen the task. I will fix that and try to add more logs if this happens again.

What I understand from the logs is that the task cancellation goes through "very quickly", and by the time we get to `assertAllCancellableTasksAreCancelled`, the tasks are unregistered. On `node_t1` the task is registered with id 18, and on `node_t0` as a child of it with id 37. There is cancelation log for task18 on t1, but no such log for task37 on t0. But there are unregistration log messages for both tasks! So my thinking is that first cancelling the task and then relying on `assertAllCancellableTasksAreCancelled` to see the state where there is at least one task on the task manager and for all seen tasks they are cancelled, might be a bit unreliable. To me it seems possible that that big assertion block could entirely miss seeing those in-between states and just see no tasks for the given action in the task manager instances. 

I was able to reproduce it locally by adding some big sleep between the cancellation and `assertAllCancellableTasksAreCancelled` call. But I am not sure it this is a reliable way of reproducing it.

If this is the case, we could at lease call the cancellation after starting the assertBusy block (i.e. `assertAllCancellableTasksAreCancelled`) (somehow in the background)? Although that doesn't fully address the assertion block missing the correct state, I think it will mitigate it a bit.
Also considering there is only one log from `assertAllCancellableTasksAreCancelled` I think missing the desired task manager state in that block is quite possible.
This seems to be the more likely reason for the failure: https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/91709#discussion_r1029601324

review_comments: I'll look into where else we might need this on master or non-master node receiving the task, and move/merge these asserts if necessary in a followup.
